title: Corridor 18 - I took an old prototyope and asked Claude to rebuild it. Should I keep going?
author: Adromakh
selftext:
Two years ago I made a rough prototype: a mobile puzzle game where a bot on a screen tells gives you instructions, and you have to figure out whether you can trust it. I liked the idea, but the prototype was clunky and I never finished it.

A weeks ago I gave it to Claude Code to see how far it could take it. This is the result: **Corridor 18**.

The game is available for test here (playable in a navigator): [https://iga-prod.itch.io/corridor-18](https://iga-prod.itch.io/corridor-18)

There is around 10 min of gameplay. I'm looking for honest opinions here. Is this idea worth pursuing? I've ton of ideas on how to push this further, but i'd like to see first if this idea can fly.

What i gave to claude: my old design document + printscreens of the game. He came with an improved version the graphics, and added sounds. I then worked on Claude to polish it, add new mechanims and the basis for a story.

comments.author: Ball_Analytics
comments.body:
I'm more concerned I understood navigator, will try it.

Edit: can't say I don't like but would definitely play it again, just don't have time atm :( also there's text leaving the box the bot types in, enraging my ocd.

replies.author: Adromakh
replies.body: My bad, I just corrected that

comments.author: JessicaTian8
comments.body: The "can you trust the robot?" idea is a nice hook — easy to explain in one line. If you keep going, maybe make a tiny playable version and watch whether people get the trust/doubt choice without instructions. Watching a few people play is usually more honest than our own opinion.

comments.author: caesium23
comments.body: Since your text auto-advances, I didn't know what to do when it's the wrong robot, so I quit.

comments.author: llothar
comments.body: It is quite a basic idea, so it has to be executed beautifuly. I'd say wiggling buttons are weird - how are physical buttons supposed to wiggle?
